mainTopic: Contradicting absent witnesses (תרי ותרי and בר שטיא), verifying signatures on a שטר, and a witness testifying from a written note or a reminder.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an argument that הכחשה, like הזמה, works only when the first witnesses are present, so the dead signers of a document cannot be contradicted. רב נחמן rejects this and rules that two witnesses against two cancel each other, so the money stays with its owner, just as in the case of בר שטיא, a man who was insane at times. In that case the property stays with בר שטיא, but only if he inherited it from his fathers. רבי אבהו rules that הזמה needs the witnesses' presence but הכחשה does not, and that a הזמה done in their absence still counts as a הכחשה. The גמרא then turns to verifying signatures on a שטר. רבי אסי allows only a שטר that was challenged and upheld in court as a sample, and the scholars of נהרדעא allow two כתובות or two field deeds held peacefully for three years. רב שימי בר אשי adds that the sample documents must come from someone else's possession, because a person cannot forge accurately from memory. Finally, a ברייתא lets a witness testify from his own written note years later. רב הונא and רבי יוחנן disagree about whether he must remember the event on his own, and the הלכה is that a fellow witness may remind him but the litigant himself may not.

steps.title: Contradiction only works in the witnesses' presence
steps.stepSummary: This compares הכחשה to הזמה. Both work only when the first witnesses are present, so the dead signers of a document cannot be contradicted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as witnesses can only be made זוממין in their presence, so too witnesses can only be contradicted in their presence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the argument of רב ששת. He compares הכחשה to הזמה to show that the dead signers' document still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that הזמה works only in the witnesses' presence. This argument stretches that rule to plain הכחשה as well. Since the signing witnesses are dead and cannot be present, the second pair's contradiction does not cancel the document.

keyTerms.meaning: Making witnesses into עדים זוממין, by showing they were somewhere else at the time
Contradicting the witnesses' account of what happened

steps.confusionAlert: הזמה and הכחשה are different things. הזמה attacks the witnesses themselves ("you were with us"). הכחשה only says the event did not happen as described. This line tries to give הכחשה the same rule as הזמה.

phrases.english: And just as we do not render the witnesses זוממין
except in their presence,
so too we do not contradict the witnesses
except in their presence.
phrases.notes: "Their" means the signers of the document, who have died and can never be present.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין מְזִימִּין אֶת הָעֵדִים אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵיהֶם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses can only be contradicted in their presence, just like הזמה, so the absent (dead) signers' document stands.

steps.title: רב נחמן: absent witnesses should be weaker, not stronger
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן argues that contradiction cancels testimony even when the witnesses are present. It makes no sense for absent witnesses, who might have admitted the truth, to be believed more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: If they were in front of us and were contradicted, that is הכחשה, and we would ignore them, because it is contradicted testimony. Now that they are not here, and if they were here maybe they would admit to the others, should they be believed?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks the previous argument. He says that being absent cannot help the witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first witnesses stood in court and were contradicted, their testimony would be thrown out. When they are absent, there is even more reason to worry, because if they came they might admit the second pair is right. So absence is no reason to trust them more, and the comparison to הזמה falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Before us, in front of the court
Pay attention to, take into account
Contradicted testimony, which we cannot rely on

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
If they were before us and were contradicted,
it would be a contradiction,
and we would not pay attention to them,
since it is contradicted testimony.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets belongs to the corrected wording, so read it as דהויא.

phrases.english: Now that they are not here,
where if they were before us
perhaps they would admit to them,
phrases.notes: Meaning the first witnesses might admit that the second pair is telling the truth.

phrases.english: are they believed?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: אִילּוּ הֲווֹ קַמַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison of הכחשה to הזמה made in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the absent signers cannot be contradicted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Present witnesses who are contradicted are thrown out. Absent witnesses, who might even admit the truth, cannot be stronger than that.

steps.title: רב נחמן: two against two, money stays with its owner
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the two pairs of witnesses cancel each other. The money stays with its current owner, just as in the case of בר שטיא's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said: Set two against two, and leave the money with its owner, just like the property of בר שטיא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his own ruling for the case. He also points to an earlier case that works the same way, which the גמרא will describe next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither pair of witnesses wins, because it is תרי ותרי. Since the document cannot be trusted, we cannot take money away from the person who holds it. The comparison to בר שטיא shows this is an established way of ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Two witnesses against two witnesses (תרי ותרי)
In the possession (חזקה) of its owner
Just as it is in, the same as

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of monetary law: when the evidence cancels out, money stays where it is.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said:
Set two against two,
and establish the money in the possession of its owner,
just as it is with the property of bar Shatya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the earlier view, רב נחמן states his own ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two witnesses contradict two, the testimonies cancel and the money stays with its present owner.

steps.title: The case of בר שטיא
steps.stepSummary: This describes the case being compared. בר שטיא sold property, one pair said he was insane at the time, and another pair said he was sane.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר שטיא sold property. Two witnesses came and said he sold it while insane. Two others came and said he sold it while healthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the case of בר שטיא that רב נחמן just mentioned. This sets up the ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר שטיא was sometimes insane and sometimes sane. If he sold while insane, the sale is void. If he sold while sane, the sale is valid. The two pairs of witnesses contradict each other exactly on this point.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who was insane at times (שוטה) and sane at other times
Insane, legally not able to make a sale

phrases.english: For bar Shatya sold property.
Two came and said:
He sold when he was insane;
and two came and said:
He sold when he was healthy.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבַר שָׁטְיָא זַבֵּין נִכְסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the case רב נחמן compared his ruling to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a case of תרי ותרי about whether a sale was made while insane or sane.

steps.title: רב אשי: the property stays with בר שטיא
steps.stepSummary: In the case of בר שטיא, the two pairs of witnesses cancel out, and the property stays with בר שטיא, its original owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Set two against two, and leave the money in the possession of בר שטיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the ruling in the case of בר שטיא. The sale is not upheld.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the witnesses cancel each other, the sale cannot be proven valid. So the property stays with its owner, בר שטיא. This is the same pattern רב נחמן used for the contradicted document.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Set two against two,
and establish the money in the possession of bar Shatya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אוֹקֵי תְּרֵי לַהֲדֵי תְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling in the case just described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With תרי ותרי over the sale, the property stays with בר שטיא.

steps.title: Only if he inherited the land from his fathers
steps.stepSummary: The ruling for בר שטיא applies only if he inherited the property. If he bought it himself, we assume he bought it while insane and sold it while insane, so he never had a strong claim to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he holds the property from his fathers. But if he does not hold it from his fathers, we say: he bought it while insane and sold it while insane.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the ruling. Whether the property goes back to בר שטיא depends on how he got it in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inherited property is firmly his, so when the witnesses cancel out, it stays with him. If he bought it himself, his purchase is just as doubtful as his sale, because both may have happened while he was insane. So he has no firm חזקה, and the buyer keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when, which limits the ruling
Possession that comes from his fathers, meaning inherited ownership

steps.whatToRemember: With תרי ותרי, money stays with its owner. But "owner" means someone with a firm claim. Someone whose own purchase is in doubt does not get that benefit.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the two words: זְבַן means he bought, and זַבֵּין means he sold. They look almost the same.

phrases.english: And we only said this
where he has possession from his fathers.
But if he does not have possession from his fathers,
we say: when he was insane he bought,
and when he was insane he sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּאִית לֵיהּ חֲזָקָה דַאֲבָהָתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב אשי's ruling to inherited property.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The property returns to בר שטיא only if he inherited it. If he bought it himself, the buyer keeps it.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: הזמה only in their presence, הכחשה even when they are absent
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו rules that הזמה can only be done in front of the first witnesses, but הכחשה works even when they are absent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Witnesses can be made זוממין only in their presence, but witnesses can be contradicted even when they are not present.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רבי אבהו, gives his ruling on the question the sugya has been discussing: does testimony against witnesses work when they are not there?
steps.deeperAnalysis: He splits the two kinds of testimony. הזמה ("you were with us somewhere else") needs the first witnesses to be present. הכחשה ("it didn't happen") works even without them.

keyTerms.meaning: Making witnesses into עדים זוממין, by testifying that they were somewhere else at the time
Contradicting witnesses, by saying the event did not happen the way they described

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up הזמה and הכחשה. In הזמה the second pair attacks the first witnesses themselves ("you were with us"). In הכחשה the second pair only disputes the facts. Different rules apply to each.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
We do not make the witnesses זוממין
except in their presence,
but we do contradict the witnesses
even not in their presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אֵין מְזִימִּין אֶת הָעֵדִים אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an independent ruling on the presence question that sits behind the earlier debate about contradicting witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הזמה requires the witnesses' presence; הכחשה does not.

steps.title: A failed הזמה still counts as a הכחשה
steps.stepSummary: If הזמה is done when the witnesses are absent, it cannot punish them as זוממין, but it still contradicts their testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for הזמה done when they are not present: even though it does not count as הזמה, it at least counts as הכחשה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו's rule is extended: an attempted הזמה done without the witnesses is not wasted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony meant as הזמה, given in the witnesses' absence, cannot bring the punishment of עדים זוממין. But it still clashes with their testimony, so it works like a הכחשה and cancels it.

phrases.english: And הזמה done not in their presence,
granted that it is not a הזמה,
it is at least a הכחשה.
phrases.notes: So the witnesses aren't punished, but their testimony is still cancelled out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲזָמָה שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵיהֶן, נְהִי דַּהֲזָמָה לָא הָוְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what happens to an attempted הזמה that fails the presence rule of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הזמה done in the witnesses' absence still works as a הכחשה.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא on checking witnesses' handwriting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the ברייתא: if the witnesses' signatures are verified some other way, their claim against the document is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If there are witnesses that this is their handwriting, or their handwriting comes from another place, from a שטר that was challenged and upheld in court, they are not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the earlier ברייתא again to set up an inference about which documents can be used to verify signatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses who say "this is our signature, but we were minors or forced" are normally believed. If their signatures can be proven another way, they lose that credibility. The ברייתא names one such way: a sample from a שטר that was challenged and upheld in court.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said": a formula for quoting a source mentioned earlier so it can be examined
A challenge or protest against a document
Was confirmed (upheld as valid) in court

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים שֶׁכְּתַב יָדָם הוּא זֶה,
phrases.english: If there are witnesses that this is their handwriting,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה כְּתַב יָדָם יוֹצֵא מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר,
phrases.english: or their handwriting comes out from another place,
from a שטר that someone challenged
and it was upheld in court,
they are not believed.
phrases.notes: The signers aren't believed when they try to cancel the document by saying they were minors or forced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים שֶׁכְּתַב יָדָם הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic by returning to the ברייתא cited earlier in the sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Signatures proven from a challenged-and-upheld שטר remove the witnesses' credibility to cancel the document.

steps.title: Only a challenged שטר works, which supports רבי אסי
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא's wording, only a challenged and upheld שטר can serve as a sample. This supports רבי אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was challenged, yes; if it was not challenged, no. This supports רבי אסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the exact wording of the ברייתא closely and finds that it backs up the view of רבי אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could simply have said "from another שטר." It says "a שטר that was challenged," so an unchallenged שטר does not count. That is exactly רבי אסי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes / No (used to draw an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: If it was challenged, yes;
if it was not challenged, no.
This supports Rabbi Asi.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרָא עָלָיו עַרְעָר — אִין, לֹא קָרָא עָלָיו עַרְעָר — לָא, מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אסי's rule that only a challenged-and-upheld שטר can verify signatures
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's specific wording "שטר שקרא עליו ערער והוחזק בבית דין"

steps.title: רבי אסי's rule for verifying a שטר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי: a שטר is verified only by comparing it to a שטר that was challenged and upheld in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אסי said: We verify a שטר only from a שטר that was challenged and upheld in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אסי's actual statement, which the ברייתא was just shown to support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing signatures needs a sample that is known to be real. A שטר that went through a court challenge and survived has proven signatures, so it is a safe sample.

keyTerms.meaning: Verifying (authenticating) a document by confirming its signatures

phrases.english: As Rabbi Asi said:
We do not verify a שטר
except from a שטר that someone challenged
and that was upheld in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי: אֵין מְקַיְּימִין אֶת הַשְּׁטָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the statement that step 10 said the ברייתא supports.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a challenged-and-upheld שטר may be used as a sample to verify signatures.

steps.title: The נהרדעי: two כתובות or two field deeds held for three years
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of נהרדעא allow verification from two כתובות, or from two deeds of fields whose owners ate the produce openly for three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars of נהרדעא say: We verify a שטר only from two כתובות, or from two fields' deeds, provided the owners ate their produce for three years undisturbed.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion gives different sources that are reliable enough to use as signature samples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These documents are accepted as samples even without a court challenge. For the field deeds there is a condition: the owners must have eaten the produce for three years (the period of חזקה) peacefully, with no protest. They require two such documents, not one.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the city נהרדעא
Three years: the period that establishes a חזקה (presumed ownership) of land

phrases.english: The scholars of Neharde'a say:
We do not verify a שטר
except from two כתובות,
or from two fields,
phrases.notes: The word "or" in square brackets is the corrected wording. The two fields means the bills of sale for two fields.

phrases.english: provided their owners ate their produce for three years,
and peacefully.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי נְהַרְדָּעֵי: אֵין מְקַיְּימִין אֶת הַשְּׁטָר אֶלָּא מִשְׁתֵּי כְּתוּבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different list of acceptable sample documents from רבי אסי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Signatures may be verified from two כתובות or from two field deeds held openly for three years.

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי: sample documents must come from someone else
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי adds that the comparison documents must come from another person's possession, not from the person using them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: And only when they come from another person's possession. But from his own possession, no.
steps.whatsHappening: An extra condition is added to the rules for verifying signatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a reliable type of sample document is not accepted if the person who wants the שטר verified brings it from his own hands. It must come from a third party.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
And only when it comes out from the possession of another.
But from his own possession, no.
phrases.notes: "His own" means the person who wants his שטר verified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: וּבְיוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יַד אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the verification rules given in steps 11–12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sample documents must come from a third party's possession.

steps.title: Why not documents from his own possession? He might forge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why one's own documents are disqualified and answers that he might have forged the signatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about his own possession that it is not accepted? Perhaps he forged them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב שימי בר אשי's rule and gives it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sample documents were in his hands, he could have practiced and forged matching signatures on both the sample and the שטר. Then the match proves nothing.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא תַּחַת יַד עַצְמוֹ דְּלָא,
phrases.english: What is different about his own possession, that it is not accepted?
Perhaps he forged.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא תַּחַת יַד עַצְמוֹ דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for and states the reasoning behind step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason documents from one's own possession cannot be used.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He may have forged the signatures while he held them.

steps.title: He could forge from someone else's documents too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: someone else's documents carry the same risk, since he could look at them and then forge.
steps.simpleTranslation: From another person's possession too: perhaps he went and saw them, came back, and forged!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason it just gave, because the same fear seems to apply to someone else's documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry is forgery, a forger could visit the third party, study the signatures, and copy them at home. So why is a third party's document any safer?

phrases.english: From the possession of another too:
perhaps he went and saw,
came back and forged!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתַּחַת יְדֵי אַחֵר נָמֵי: דִּלְמָא אֲזַל וַחֲזָא, אֲתָא וְזַיֵּיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 14 by applying it to the third-party case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי בר אשי's distinction between one's own documents and another's
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The forgery concern applies equally when the documents are with someone else, since he could view them and forge later.

steps.title: He cannot copy that accurately from memory
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a person cannot forge signatures that precisely from memory alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He cannot be that precise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps רב שימי בר אשי's rule in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forging well needs the original in front of you. Someone who only looked at another person's document cannot reproduce the signature exactly enough to fool the court, so third-party documents are safe.

keyTerms.meaning: To be precise, to get it exactly right

steps.whatToRemember: To verify a שטר, the court compares signatures only to reliable samples: a שטר challenged and upheld in court (רבי אסי), or two כתובות or two field deeds held for three years (נהרדעי). The samples must come from a third party, because a person could forge with the documents in hand but not from memory.

phrases.english: He is not able to be precise to such an extent.
phrases.notes: He means copying from memory after just seeing them, without the documents in front of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלֵּי הַאי לָא מָצֵי מְכַוֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical distinction: having the documents in hand versus copying from memory
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forgery is equally possible whether or not the documents are in his possession.
steps.terutzMaskana: Precise forgery requires the original in hand. From memory it cannot be done accurately, so third-party documents are reliable.

steps.title: A witness may testify from his own written record years later
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a person may write his testimony in a document and later testify based on it, even many years afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person may write his testimony on a document and testify about it even after several years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. It says a witness may write down what he saw and use that record to testify much later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows a written note to support a witness's testimony after a long time has passed. It does not say whether the witness must still remember the event. The next two steps argue about exactly that point.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A person may write his testimony on a document,
phrases.notes: He means a private note the witness writes for himself so he won't forget what he saw.

phrases.english: and testify about it
even after several years.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from checking signatures to a witness's memory.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness may testify based on his own written record, even years later.

steps.title: רב הונא: only if he remembers on his own
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the ברייתא. The witness may use his note only if he still remembers the event himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: This applies only if he remembers it on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds a condition to the ברייתא. In his view the written note can only refresh a memory the witness already has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב הונא, the note is only a memory aid and cannot replace the witness's own knowledge. If the witness has completely forgotten the event, he may not testify from the paper alone.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when. It introduces a condition.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
And this is only if he remembers it on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: וְהוּא שֶׁזּוֹכְרָהּ מֵעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Written testimony is valid only as a reminder for a witness who still remembers the event.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even if he does not remember
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב הונא. The witness may testify from his note even if he does not remember the event on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Even if he does not remember it on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reads the ברייתא more broadly than רב הונא does. The witness may testify even if he only remembers the event after reading his note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the witness does not need to remember the event without help. A memory that comes back only through the written note still allows him to testify. This sets up רבה's practical conclusion in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין זוֹכְרָהּ מֵעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: Even if he does not remember it on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין זוֹכְרָהּ מֵעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness may testify from his written record even if he remembers the event only through the record, not on his own.

steps.title: רבה: one witness may remind the other
steps.stepSummary: רבה learns from רבי יוחנן that if one of two witnesses forgets the testimony, the other witness may remind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Learn from רבי יוחנן's view that if two people know some testimony and one of them forgets, one may remind the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה takes רבי יוחנן's view and applies it to a new case. One witness may jog his fellow witness's memory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן accepts testimony even when the witness's memory comes back only through an outside prompt, his written note. So a reminder from a fellow witness works the same way. The forgetful witness may then testify, even though his memory came back through someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, conclude from it

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Learn from the view of Rabbi Yochanan:
These two people who know some testimony
and one of them forgot it,
one may remind his fellow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule from רבי יוחנן's position in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One witness may remind his fellow witness of testimony the fellow forgot.

steps.title: What if the litigant himself reminds the witness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a question. If the person who benefits from the testimony reminds the witness, may the witness still testify?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: If he himself reminds the witness, what is the ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by raising a new question. A fellow witness may remind him, but what about the litigant himself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fellow witness has no personal stake, but the litigant does. The question is whether a reminder from an interested party is still acceptable. The next steps give two answers.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them, the Sages

steps.confusionAlert: Here עצמו no longer means the witness remembering on his own, as in steps 18 and 19. It now means the litigant himself, the person whose case it is, giving the reminder.

phrases.english: A question was asked:
If he himself reminds the witness, what is the ruling?
phrases.notes: Himself means the litigant, the person who gains from this testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: עַצְמוֹ, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבה's case to a reminder given by an interested party.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the litigant himself may remind a forgetful witness.

steps.title: רב חביבא: even the litigant himself may remind him
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא says that even the litigant himself may remind the witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rav Chaviva said: Even he himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חביבא gives the first answer. A reminder from the litigant is also acceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חביבא treats any reminder the same way, as long as the witness now truly remembers. In his view, the litigant's interest in the case does not disqualify the reminder.

phrases.english: Rav Chaviva said:
Even he himself may remind him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֲבִיבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The litigant may remind the witness, and the witness may testify.

steps.title: מר בריה דרב אשי: not the litigant himself
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרב אשי disagrees. The litigant himself may not remind the witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרב אשי said: Not he himself.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בריה דרב אשי gives the opposite answer. A reminder from the litigant is not acceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fellow witness has nothing to gain, but the litigant does. His reminder could shape what the witness says. So the witness may not rely on it.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Rav Ashi, said:
He himself may not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: עַצְמוֹ לֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב חביבא in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The litigant may not remind the witness.

steps.title: The הלכה: the litigant may not remind the witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like מר בריה דרב אשי. The litigant himself may not remind the witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: not he himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the dispute and closes this topic. The litigant may not jog the witness's memory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The final ruling follows מר בריה דרב אשי. A fellow witness may remind a forgetful witness, as רבה taught, but the interested party may not.
steps.whatToRemember: A fellow witness may remind a witness who forgot, but the litigant himself may not, and the הלכה follows this.
steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, a witness's memory may be refreshed by a fellow witness but not by the person who gains from the testimony.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: he himself may not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא עַצְמוֹ לֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute between steps 22 and 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The litigant may not remind the witness, and the הלכה follows מר בריה דרב אשי.
